Title: How a centrist outsider became New Zealand's kingmaker
Article:
FIFTEEN months after spotting a job ad seeking a new leader for a political party, Qiulae Wong will help decide New Zealand's next government after Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's right-wing coalition lost its majority.
The 38-year-old former KPMG consultant took over a party polling at about one per cent in August last year.
Since then, the Opportunity Party has secured seven seats and 6.1 per cent of the vote in this month's election, placing it in prime position to play kingmaker as Luxon rushes to piece together a workable coalition.
Wong preaches "pragmatic politics" as a counter to growing polarisation, saying she wants to "bring the heat down a little bit and actually just focus on moving the country forward."
Establishment parties worldwide have been losing support in recent elections, replaced by a surge in populist movements touting more radical policies on the left or right.
But Wong, who is of Chinese and European descent and was born in Fiji, said following the election she believed the result showed voters were tiring of that kind of politics.
"I think we are seeing a push globally for more pragmatic politics," she told journalists.
"We've seen that populism doesn't deliver results," she said.
"It is paper thin; it doesn't have substance around taking countries forward.
"So it's really encouraging to have had that support."
Wong worked in sustainable fashion before entering politics.
A mother of two, her social media emphasises her ordinariness – moving effortlessly from pints in the sun and ice creams with the kids to political rallies and media events.
All that has prompted comparisons to former prime minister Jacinda Ardern, whose star power made her a global progressive icon.
"I think the way in which both of those two relatively young women are attempting a different style of politics is something that marks Wong apart," Massey University politics professor Richard Shaw told AFP.
He said Opportunity's rise had been 'remarkable', given its differences to other New Zealand political parties and due to the relative inexperience of Wong.
"At a time when the politics of this country are becoming more fraught and more feral and more shouty, and there is horrendous online trolling of women in public life, you've got this woman who's coming in saying 'I'm leading a party and we're going to do it this way'.
"I think that appeals to people."
Luxon had previously ruled out working with Opportunity.
He now faces an embarrassing volte-face, admitting Friday he will need the centrist outsiders' support if he wants to stay in office.
All eyes are now on Wong as the country faces weeks of political wrangling.
She has said she will work with Luxon – but insisted that her party's 'bottom lines' are non-negotiable.
Those lines – on climate change action, regulations on political lobbying, healthcare reform, phasing out bottom trawling, and cost of living – could be a hard sell in talks with Luxon's right-wing partners, the populist NZ First and libertarian ACT.
On the campaign trail, she also ruled out working with a government in which NZ First leader Winston Peters was foreign minister, after he told a Chinese-born lawmaker to 'go back to your own country.'
And on Friday she refused to rule out taking the country back for a second election if talks don't work out.
"All we can do is be as constructive and proactive as possible to make this happen. But it's not just us around the table," she said.

Title: Saudi strike kills 11 in Yemen - Houthi media
Article:
SANAA: A Saudi strike killed 11 people on Friday in Yemen, Houthi media said, as the Saudi-led coalition fighting the group said it shot down a drone targeting Riyadh.
The latest incidents came a day after a deadly Houthi attack on a Saudi oil refinery, and add to a growing tally of violence since Yemen's civil war reignited over the summer.
The coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government against the Iran-allied Houthis, has been regularly bombing areas under their control.
In response, Houthi forces have been targeting the oil-rich kingdom almost daily, hitting energy facilities, airports and the financial district of the capital, Riyadh.
Saudi warplanes carried out a raid on a residential building in the city of Al-Turba in Taiz governorate on Friday, killing "11 citizens, most of them children", the Houthis' Saba news agency said, citing a local source.
The agency also reported strikes targeting fuel tanks in the Saada region, the movement's birthplace and stronghold.
On Thursday, the Houthis targeted the Jazan refinery in southern Saudi Arabia, killing a Nepalese worker and injuring several other people, according to the Saudi Press Agency (SPA).
The attack also triggered a fire that led to the shutdown of the facility, SPA said.
Yemen plunged back into war in July, after years of relative calm, opening a new front in the Middle East war.
Hostilities intensified in September when the Houthis, who already controlled Yemen's most densely populated areas, seized the western coastline overlooking the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait on the Red Sea.
The Houthis are now advancing toward Aden, a major southern city where the government has taken refuge after being driven out of the capital Sanaa in 2015.
Since the conflict resumed, fighting in Yemen has killed more than 2,300 people and displaced over 364,000, according to the United Nations.
Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia have killed 27 people, according to the kingdom's authorities.

Title: NST Leader: Ensuring a resilient food supply chain
Article:
PEOPLE in Malaysia are linked by the common thread of bountiful food, dominated by the ubiquity of local delicacies.
Local and foreign foodies and influencers wax lyrical on the country's epicurean delights, analyse  recipes and spotlight  chefs, turning them into mini-superstars.   But in celebrating Malaysia's melting pot of global dishes, little attention is placed on how the raw food material is actually sourced.
The country remains a supreme gourmet paradise chiefly because of  affordability and supply stability.
This is underlined by Malaysia's rank of 10th out of 60 countries on the inaugural Resilient Food Systems Index released this year. It also holds 6.23 months of physical rice stockpiles (1.05 million  tonnes) to ensure short-term availability and help maintain stable prices.
Malaysia is self-sufficient in 23 commodities, including  duck meat and eggs, tropical fruits, poultry and fish.
Yet, there is still  concern over the  rising import bill for key staples.   Last year, Malaysia spent RM93.7 billion on importing mutton (with the import dependency rate at 90.7 per cent), beef (82.6 per cent), rice (45 per cent) and temperate vegetables.
Local farming is heavily reliant on imported fertiliser and  sensitive to feed price fluctuations, while extreme weather, such as floods  and a forecasted Super El Niño next year, is also a  concern.
They have already been cited as factors behind  Malaysia's padi output falling  4.5 per cent  below the national five-year average this year.
In the next 10 years, the National Agrofood Policy 2021-2030 and phased  import-reduction road maps  intend to reduce the import bill by 13 per cent, or RM93.7 billion, annually.
To meet this goal, Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu announced an ambitious plan to increase padi yields in  Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) areas to 10 tonnes per hectare by 2030.
This target is attainable through modern technology, improved fertilisation and better farming practices.
Mada covers 100,685ha across the rice bowls of Kedah and Perlis, the nation's largest granary area accounting for 40 per cent of its rice production.
In comparison, Thailand averages 2.85 to three tonnes per hectare nationally across 10 to 11 million ha.
Malaysia's rice authorities are rolling out drones, technical and vocational education and  training and better fertilisation practices while continuing to  provide RM2.6 billion in subsidies for local production to boost productivity.
Each extra tonne per hectare adds RM500 for farmers.   Of course, there are obstacles: Mada averages only five to 5.22 tonnes per hectare, a two per cent yield increase in the latest season.
To double the average by 2030, Mada needs rapid, widespread adoption rather than isolated gains, swifter modernisation and better preparation against the elements.  And to somehow make farming "cool" for the next generation.

Title: Chandra Muzaffar's contributions to reformasi, PKR will be remembered, says Fuziah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The death of academic and civil society activist Dr Chandra Muzaffar is a major loss to the country, particularly Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR), which recognises his contributions to the reform movement and the party's formation.
PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said Chandra was among those who courageously championed justice during the reformasi movement in 1998, despite facing various pressures and challenges.
She said he had played an important role through his involvement in various civil society organisations and the country's political arena.
"From his involvement in Gerakan Keadilan Rakyat Malaysia (Gerak), to serving as deputy president of the Social Justice Movement (Adil), and later becoming the first deputy president of Parti Keadilan Nasional in 1999, he helped sow the seeds of the struggle that laid the foundation for the PKR we know today.
"As someone who also went through the early days of this struggle, I deeply appreciate all his services, sacrifices and intellectual contributions.
"It was not easy to build a political party in such challenging circumstances at the time," she said in a Facebook post today.
Fuziah said Chandra's contributions extended beyond politics to include the pursuit of social justice, human rights, humanitarian causes and harmony across races, religions and nations.
She said Chandra was also the founder of Aliran Kesedaran Negara (Aliran) and a key figure behind the International Movement for a Just World (Just), dedicating his life to the pursuit of universal justice.
Fuziah said his services and sacrifices would remain etched in the history of the reformasi movement and PKR.
She also extended her condolences to his family and prayed for his soul to be blessed.
"May Allah SWT forgive his sins, accept his good deeds, grant him peace in his grave and place him among the faithful and righteous.
"Farewell, Dr Chandra. Thank you for helping sow the seeds of this struggle," she said.

Title: The algorithms that power our social media addiction
Article:
SOCIAL media algorithms are a powerful feature of online life, serving up content to users based on their browsing habits or personal data.
Users in Australia will be able to opt out of them in a year's time, under new legislation approved in parliament that also imposes fines on tech giants if they fail to remove content deemed harmful.
Open TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube or other platforms, and you'll see a scrolling feed or recommendations bar showing content targeted to your interests.
These posts are selected for users based on programming rules called algorithms that predict what you will engage with — whether it's something you like, or that riles you.
Broadly speaking, the recommendations are based on what the machine knows about you: what you've interacted with or posted about online, or information such as your age, job, location and marital status.
Social media giants usually keep the coding behind these algorithms —  the so-called "secret sauce" that drives traffic to their platforms —  closely guarded.
It's a familiar pattern for many — open your phone on a break and before you know it, an hour has passed and you're still scrolling.
That's by design, researchers and activists say.
"These platforms have engineered addictive features that keep children and adults online longer than they intend, often at the expense of sleep, well-being and real-world connection," said Mark Williams, honorary professor of cognitive neuroscience at Macquarie University.
In a landmark trial in Los Angeles this year, tech giants were accused of creating "addiction machines".
Experts point to strategies companies use to encourage scrolling, like never-ending feeds, intermittent rewards and time-sensitive notifications.
"This unpredictability triggers the dopamine system, creating a compulsive cycle of seeking and anticipation," University of Leicester lecturer Quynh Hoang wrote.
Such dependence is similar to substance addiction, research published in online medical journal Cureus last year found.
By pushing people to content they respond to emotionally, many say social media can drive us into "rabbit holes" that are difficult to escape.
The recommendations "are designed to hold our attention, and too often that means privileging provocative and extreme content because outrage drives engagement and engagement drives profit", said Steven Roberts at Monash University.
Algorithms have been accused of pushing teenage boys towards the "manosphere" — communities and influencers that promote misogyny and violence against women.
Research from Melbourne-based men's health charity Movember found that social media guided young men to that content whether they wanted it or not, a path leading from innocuous posts about working out and sports to violent, extreme content.
"We can already see the consequences in Australian schools," where "misogyny is rife", Roberts said.
"Our national survey of more than 2,600 teachers found that... 70 per cent had frequently or occasionally seen the impact of manosphere social media influencers present on student attitudes and behaviour."
Under Australia's new rules, social media giants must allow users to "opt out" of the algorithm.
They also hold the firms responsible for protecting under-18s from pornography, online bullying and content that glorifies crime or encourages eating disorders.
The "my feed, my way" initiative aims to bring social media back to basics —  a feed focused on updates from friends, family and pages you follow.
"The government has handed Australians a switch. Whether anyone flips it is another matter," said Lisa Harrison, a lecturer in communication and media at Flinders University.
In a survey last year of over 6,000 people in six countries, only one in five said they would switch off personalised recommendations if they could, she noted.
"The algorithm is good at its job, and the minority who do opt out will find a feed of friends and creators feels quieter than the one they left."

Title: NST wins two gold awards at MPRA 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The New Straits Times (NST) clinched two gold awards at the 18th Malaysia Public Relations Awards (MPRA) 2026, with its editor and writer Intan Maizura Ahmad Kamal taking home both accolades.
Intan, who is Life and Times and Sunday Vibes editor, won gold in the Lifestyle Print category for her article, "A Professor's Love Letter to Malaysia — In Poems and Pawprints".
She also received gold in the Op-Ed Writing Print category for "While They're Still at the Door".
"I didn't expect to win two golds tonight. It's an honour, and especially sweet after my recent Perkeso win just weeks ago," she said.
Intan dedicated the awards to the NST team and congratulated the other recipients.
NST group editor and Media Prima Berhad deputy group managing editor (News and Current Affairs) Datuk Farrah Naz Karim, who was among the judging panel, also received a token of appreciation.
In his address, Public Relations and Communications Association of Malaysia (PRCA Malaysia) president Prof Mohd Said Bani C.M. Din said technological shifts had changed how people communicated but not the foundations of trust.
He said experienced practitioners brought knowledge and perspective, while younger communicators contributed fresh thinking and digital fluency.
"The future of PR belongs to those who bridge both.
"AI can generate content and amplify messages, but none can replace genuine human understanding, empathy and authentic relationships," he said.
Among the other winners was RTM's Mohan Chinnasamy, who won gold in the Social Responsibility (Broadcast) category for "WCE: West Coast Expressway".
Bernama's Norhidayyu Zainal received gold in the Lifestyle Coverage Online category for "Kucing Jadi Pencerita Teroka Malaysia Dalam Buku Puisi Kembara".
RTM's Haryati Hani Ab Aziz won silver in the Lifestyle Coverage Online category for "KL Ada Hutan dan Burung Tropika?"
RTM director-general of Broadcasting Datuk Ashwad Ismail received the PRCA Malaysia Leadership Award.
Also present were Malaysian Press Institute president Datuk Yong Soo Heong, Scoop managing editor Terence Fernandez, and DagangNews managing editor Johardy Ibrahim.

Title: A year of high-stakes polls could upend Europe
Article:
WHAT  will tomorrow's Europe look like? The answer may hinge on a looming year of back-to-back elections, with France at centre stage, that could change the face of the European Union and potentially jam its decision-making.
Between now and the end of next year, four of the EU's five largest countries will choose new leaders in contests marked by the rise of eurosceptic forces — groups wary of Brussels' influence which seek to grant more power to individual member states.
It will be an unprecedented series of political tests for the bloc.
The most consequential vote takes place in April and May in France, where far-right leader Marine Le Pen is running in the lead.
Depending on the outcome in France and elsewhere, "what we risk is paralysis" in European decision-making, summed up one Brussels diplomat, granted anonymity to discuss the sensitive matter.
The high-stakes electoral cycle kicks off tomorrow  in Spain. Shaped by heated debates over immigration and housing, that vote could end the era of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.
After more than eight years in power, Sanchez is one of the last remaining socialist leaders in the 27-nation bloc, often at odds with his counterparts, including on migration and defence.
Most polls show him losing to conservative rival Alberto Nunez Feijoo.
The vote could also see the far right enter government for the first time since Francisco Franco's dictatorship ended in 1975, with the Vox party seeking to play kingmaker.
Looking into next year, close attention will focus on Italy, where hard-right leader Giorgia Meloni faces a challenge on her right flank from former general Roberto Vannacci, an anti-migration hawk opposed to military aid for Ukraine.
And Brussels will be scrutinising parliamentary elections in Poland, set for a new showdown between the camp of pro-European Prime Minister Donald Tusk and that of nationalist President Karol Nawrocki.
Next year will also bring elections in a host of smaller EU nations, such as Estonia — an ardent backer of Ukraine which accuses Russia of targeting it with a campaign of sabotage.
Polls are likewise scheduled in Greece, Finland and Slovakia, where Prime Minister Robert Fico maintains friendly ties with the Kremlin.
But no race is causing more concern in Brussels than the French presidential race.
Frontrunner Le Pen is pushing a vision for Europe in stark contrast to the one championed by President Emmanuel Macron over the past decade.
The National Rally (RN) leader has made clear she would shelve plans for further EU enlargement and pull the plug on funding for Ukraine.
Le Pen recently travelled to Brussels to make her case, vowing to pare back the European Commission to a "secretariat" serving member states and slash France's contribution to the EU budget.
Celia Belin, of the European Council on Foreign Relations, said Le Pen's "radical" policies on Europe "would be putting France on a collision path with EU institutions".
The bloc's top officials have yet to establish meaningful contacts with Le Pen, making it all the more difficult to predict the knock-on effects her election could have in Brussels.
It is an open question how discussions among the bloc's 27 leaders might unfold during late-night European summits, if a victorious Le Pen decided to play hardball.
With German Chancellor Friedrich Merz already weakened in Berlin, would her election cause the EU's decision-making machinery to grind to a halt?
Could commission chief Ursula von der Leyen suffer the consequences? Some in Brussels are already gaming out worst-case scenarios.
Others prefer to downplay Le Pen's statements, arguing that if she comes to power, she will have little choice but to work within the EU framework —  as did Italy's Meloni.
"Not everything has to be the end of the world," countered one diplomat. "If there is a vacuum, other countries will fill the gap."
Others caution against reading too much into polling, arguing eurosceptic forces may fail to convert momentum into votes.
But officials and diplomats AFP spoke to broadly agreed on one thing: the EU needs to bolster its ability to weather electoral shocks in the months ahead.
That effort starts now with hard-fought negotiations to agree the bloc's next seven-year budget, and to secure funding for Ukraine through next year.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SPM 2026: Examinations Board files report over alleged leaked papers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Examinations Board (LP) has lodged a report with the authorities following the spread of claims about leaked 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination papers.
In a statement today, LP said the report was lodged to facilitate further investigations and enable appropriate action to be taken under existing laws.
"LP takes seriously the spread of information concerning alleged leaks of 2026 SPM examination papers.
"Based on information circulating on social media platform Threads, posted by several users believed to be examination candidates, the issue is suspected to involve a modus operandi used by individuals carrying out scams.
"The intention is to exploit candidates' anxieties and desire to obtain excellent examination results," it said.
Earlier, media reports said claims of a leaked SPM Moral Education paper that went viral on social media two days ago were found not to meet the definition of an examination paper leak.
The assessment was based on the National Assessment Policy, Third Edition 2023.
Checks found that the post was uploaded at 11.44am, after the Moral Education examination had ended at 10.45am.
LP said it would not hesitate to lodge reports with the authorities against anyone spreading baseless claims of examination paper leaks that could cause anxiety among candidates, parents and the public.
"LP advises candidates, parents and the public to remain vigilant, avoid falling for offers to sell examination papers and refrain from spreading unverified information.
"LP remains committed to safeguarding the security, confidentiality, integrity and credibility of public examinations to ensure fairness for all candidates," it said.

Title: Barista claims trial to rape of 15-year-old girl, possession of obscene material
Article:
AYER KEROH: A barista was charged at the Sessions Court and magistrate's court here today with three offences, including raping a minor and possessing child pornography and obscene material.
Hidayatullah Tawadhu, 22, pleaded not guilty to all charges and claimed trial in separate proceedings before Sessions Court judge Rohatul Akmar Abdullah and magistrate Nur Afiqah Radhiah Zainurin.
At the Sessions Court, he was charged with raping a 15-year-old girl at a cafe near the Tiang Dua junction here on Sept 23 at 8.17pm.
The charge was framed under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
On the second charge, he was accused of possessing child pornography in the form of obscene videos and photographs at the same premises on Aug 31 at 2.50pm.
He was charged under Section 10 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which carries a maximum jail term of 5 years, a fine of up to RM10,000, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Nor Asnini Kamarudin proposed bail of RM40,000 for the two charges.
However, Rohatul Akmar did not make an order on bail as no one was present to stand as surety for the accused.
The court fixed Jan 15, 2027, for mention.
Meanwhile, at the Magistrate's Court, Hidayatullah faced a separate charge of possessing a mobile phone containing obscene material for distribution.
The offence was allegedly committed at the Melaka Contingent Police Headquarters on Nov 23 at 8.59pm.
He was charged under Section 292 of the Penal Code, which provides for a jail term of up to three years, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Noor Syazwani Mohamad Yusri prosecuted the case, which was fixed for mention on Jan 11, 2027.

Title: Five containers suspected of carrying e-waste found to contain metal scrap
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Five containers suspected of carrying electronic waste (e-waste) at Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP) in Gelang Patah were found to contain metal scrap instead.
The Johor Department of Environment (DOE) said the finding followed physical inspections of the containers by its Scheduled Waste Enforcement Unit.
The integrated enforcement operation was conducted in cooperation with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department's CCU unit in Gelang Patah and attended by representatives of the importing company.
"Checks on the import documents also confirmed that the goods complied with the stipulated criteria and were accompanied by a valid Certificate of Approval (COA) from Sirim Berhad.
"This confirms that the cargo in all five containers comprised metal scrap and not electronic waste as initially suspected," it said in a Facebook post today.
The department said Malaysia, as a member of the Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and Their Disposal, was bound by strict international procedures.
It said the importation of scheduled waste without written approval from the Director-General of Environmental Quality was a serious offence under Section 34B of the Environmental Quality Act 1974 (Amendment 2024).
"Those found guilty may face severe legal action, including mandatory imprisonment and a fine of up to RM10 million.
"The containers may also be ordered to be returned immediately to their country of origin if they are found to contain scheduled waste imported without approval," it said.
The department said it would continue working with strategic partners at the country's entry points and intensify enforcement operations to curb attempts to smuggle hazardous waste and protect the country's environmental sustainability.
Members of the public with information on environmental pollution can lodge complaints through the toll-free line at 1-800-88-2727, email aduan_k@doe.gov.my or the DOE's e-Aduan portal.

Title: Three armed men rob Kajang goldsmith shop in supermarket
Article:
KAJANG: Police are tracking down three armed men who robbed a goldsmith shop inside a supermarket in Bandar Teknologi Kajang here today.
Kajang police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said preliminary investigations found that the suspects were armed with parangs and hammers.
"The suspects fled on two motorcycles after carrying out the robbery at 2.23pm.
"The total losses incurred in the incident are still being investigated," he said in a statement.
Naazron said the case was being investigated under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code for gang robbery with dangerous weapons.
Upon conviction, the offences carry a jail term of up to 20 years and whipping.
Those with information about the incident are urged to contact investigating officer Inspector Muhammad Nabil Aizat at 013-6232713 or visit the nearest police station.
Earlier, closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage of the incident went viral on social media, showing the suspects, dressed in dark clothing and wearing helmets, walking briskly through the supermarket concourse near an escalator before heading towards the goldsmith shop.
The robbery, which took place during the supermarket's operating hours, startled members of the public and workers at nearby premises who witnessed the incident.

Title: Beyond the beep: The operation behind MySiren
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A mobile phone alert may appear simple, but delivering emergency warnings across affected areas requires extensive technology and close coordination between government agencies and telecommunications operators.
Malaysia's Early Warning System (EWS), known as MySiren, uses Cell Broadcast System (CBS) technology to transmit alerts simultaneously to compatible mobile phones within designated geographical areas.
Developed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), the system provides emergency warnings without requiring users to download an application or subscribe to a service.
According to MCMC, alerts may cover threats to life, health, safety or property, including floods, severe weather, tsunamis, major fires and hazardous materials incidents.
To receive alerts, iPhones must be iPhone 11 or newer models running iOS 27.2 or later. Compatible Android devices require Android 12 or later, while Huawei devices must run EMUI 16 or later.
Devices must also support CBS and be connected to participating 4G or 5G mobile networks.
The system complements existing warning channels, including SMS, radio and television broadcasts, sirens and announcements by local authorities.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil previously said SMS alerts would continue to be used for phones that did not support the new system.
Unlike SMS, which delivers messages individually to phone numbers, CBS broadcasts alerts through selected mobile network cells.
When an emergency occurs, authorised agencies use MySiren to issue warnings targeting specific geographical areas, depending on the nature and location of the threat.
The alerts are then transmitted through telecommunications networks to designated cell sites, which broadcast them to compatible phones within their coverage areas.
Much like a loudspeaker addressing everyone within earshot, CBS delivers a single warning to multiple phones simultaneously without having to contact each recipient individually.
According to MCMC, alerts can reach devices in less than a minute, compared to up to an hour or longer for bulk SMS notifications.
CBS also does not require mobile data or an Internet connection, allowing alerts to reach compatible devices even when networks are congested.
The warning appears as an emergency notification on the phone screen, accompanied by a distinctive alarm sound and vibration, even when the device is set to silent.
Behind the system's implementation is extensive coordination involving MCMC, the National Disaster Management Agency, other disaster management agencies and telecommunications service providers to ensure alerts reach devices across different networks.
Public awareness is equally important, as recipients must be able to recognise official warnings and understand how to respond.
While social media can spread emergency information quickly, it also allows misinformation and unverified reports to circulate, potentially creating confusion during critical situations.
The public is advised to always refer to official channels for accurate and reliable information.
Ultimately, MySiren's effectiveness depends not only on the technology used to deliver alerts, but also on the coordination behind the system and the public's ability to respond appropriately.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid hopes appointment of 6 Negri Sembilan Exco members ends political crisis
Article:
BAGAN DATUK: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi hopes the appointment of six Negri Sembilan state executive council (Exco) members today will bring an end to the political crisis in the state.
Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister and Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said Umno and BN were grateful for the consent given by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, to the new Exco line-up.
He said the appointments would enable the state government to resume its responsibilities, including convening a special budget sitting of the State Legislative Assembly and delivering services to the people.
"Most importantly, we want the people to have confidence in the government following Tuanku's consent.
"I am confident the crisis has ended, and we hope no new problems will arise after this," he told reporters after officiating the 26K Huffaz 2026 Gathering and Bagan Datuk Bermunajat event at Masjid Tuminah Hamidi here today.
Zahid said five senior party leaders had an audience with Tuanku Muhriz yesterday to seek the best solution for the state's stability.
They were Zahid, Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
He called on the people of Negri Sembilan to respect and support decisions made with the consent of the palace.
"A calm discussion was held, and what Tuanku decided is the best decision. The people as a whole must support what has been consented to and Tuanku's decree," he said.
Earlier today, six assemblymen were sworn in as Negri Sembilan Exco members before Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Besar Seri Menanti in Kuala Pilah.
They are Suhaimi Aini (Kota), Datuk Mohd Zaidy Abdul Kadir (Jeram Padang), Ridzuan Ahmad (Gemas), Abdul Fatah Zakaria (Bagan Pinang), Mohamad Qayyum Abd Jalil (Senaling) and Koh Kim Swee (Repah).
The appointments mark a change to the previous 10-member Exco line-up following the political crisis in the state, which emerged after 24 Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional assemblymen reached a consensus to abide by their respective party leaderships' decisions.

Title: Bintulu Port estimates RM148mil reduction in AmanahRaya IM funds carrying value
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd is assessing the potential impact of an estimated RM147.91 million reduction in the carrying value of its investments in two AmanahRaya Investment Management Sdn Bhd (ARIM)-managed unit trust funds.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the port operator said the reduction arose after Zetrix AI Bhd failed to make a payment due on its sukuk on Nov 6, 2026.
MARC Ratings subsequently downgraded the sukuk to D IS, prompting ARIM to revalue the sukuk to nil.
The investments involve AmanahRaya Syariah Trust Fund (ARSTF) and AmanahRaya Syariah Income Fund (ARSIF), both managed by ARIM, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Amanah Raya Bhd.
As at Nov 26, 2026, the group's total investments in ARSTF and ARSIF amounted to RM205.57 million and RM198.02 million respectively.
Their corresponding carrying values stood at RM193.93 million and RM160.94 million respectively.
The company said the estimated reduction followed a decline in the net asset value of approximately 32.3 per cent for ARSTF and 25.75 per cent for ARSIF, as communicated by ARIM.
The estimated reduction in carrying values between Nov 6 and Nov 10 amounted to RM92.24 million for ARSTF and RM55.67 million for ARSIF.
The corresponding estimated carrying values as at Nov 10 stood at RM193.34 million and RM160.45 million respectively.
Bintulu Port said the figures were unaudited and indicative, subject to the funds' final valuation and the group's year-end accounting process.
"The group is closely monitoring developments and assessing their potential implications for the group's investments, including any impact on their liquidity, valuation and recoverability.
"The group will also pursue all available avenues to recover any losses that may arise from its investments in the funds," it said.

Title: Bintulu Port's Q3 net profit fell 51pc; AmanahRaya IM funds impact in Q4
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd's net profit fell 50.8 per cent to RM15.87 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY2026), from RM32.22 million a year earlier.
The board recommended a third interim single-tier dividend of four sen per share, amounting to RM18.4 million, for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026.
The dividend brings the total interim dividend for the financial year to 10 sen per share.
The decline in profits for the quarter was partly due to 17.8 per cent increase in total expenditure to RM206.36 million from RM175.12 million a year ago due to higher repair and maintenance, fuel, and manpower costs, alongside lower non-operating income.
The decline of net profit came despite higher revenue, which rose 7.6 per cent to RM219.88 million from RM204.43 million in the corresponding quarter last year.
Bintulu Port also revealed that it holds RM403.59 million in two AmanahRaya Investment Management unit trust funds, namely AmanahRaya Syariah Trust Fund and and AmanahRaya Syariah Income Fund that were exposed to the Zetrix AI Bhd sukuk default on Nov 6.
The sukuk revaluation to nil resulted in an estimated RM147.91 million reduction in carrying value between Nov 6 and Nov 10, which will be recognised as a non-cash fair value loss in Q4 FY2026.
In its Bursa Malaysia filing, the group said higher revenue from port services and bulking facilities supported its quarterly performance.
"Revenue from operations at Samalaju Industrial Port of RM48.47 million is higher by RM5.38 million compared to RM43.09 million recorded in the corresponding quarter mainly due to handling of manganese ore, quartz and alumina," it said.
Meanwhile, revenue from bulking facilities rose to RM12.04 million from RM11.41 million in the same quarter last year.
For the first nine months of financial year 2026, net profit declined 20.3 per cent to RM76.03 million. Revenue, however, increased 8.8 per cent to RM653.92 million.
The group said higher LNG cargo handling and supply base activities contributed to Bintulu Port's revenue growth, which increased 9.3 per cent to RM483.88 million.
Samalaju Industrial Port generated RM134.70 million in revenue, compared with RM126.97 million previously, mainly driven by higher manganese ore handling.
Revenue from bulking facilities also increased to RM35.34 million from RM31.09 million.
However, expenditure for the nine-month period rose to RM574.22 million from RM511.15 million, mainly due to higher direct operating costs, port maintenance and manpower expenses.
Looking ahead, the handling of LNG cargoes and vessel calls will remain the group's key revenue contributor, supported by the handling of other liquid bulk cargoes at Bintulu Port and bulk cargoes at Samalaju Port.

Title: MCMC's RM600mil suit against Google papers served on local lawyers, says Teo
Article:
KULAI: The legal papers for the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission's (MCMC) RM600 million lawsuit against Google LLC have been served on the company's lawyers in Malaysia.
The legal action stems from allegations that the platform failed to curb online gambling content and other unlawful material on YouTube.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the lawsuit also included claims for manpower costs incurred by the commission in monitoring content on behalf of the technology company.
She said legal action was taken after the platform's content moderation and response mechanisms were found to be unsatisfactory in removing criminal content in Malaysia.
"The lawsuit has been served on Google's lawyers in Malaysia. MCMC decided to sue Google not only to seek damages but also to claim for the manpower required to lodge reports with YouTube.
"Google should have its own team to moderate this harmful content.
"When MCMC has to monitor the content and submit reports, we are essentially doing the work on Google's behalf," she told reporters after officiating the Aspirasi Madani and Year Six Appreciation programme at Sekolah Kebangsaan Murni Jaya, Kampung Murni Jaya, Layang-Layang, here today.
MCMC had earlier filed two legal actions against Google LLC, seeking total damages of RM600 million over alleged failures to address harmful online content on YouTube.
The first suit concerns Google's alleged failure to tackle online gambling content, while the second relates to the republication of unlawful content by Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo.
For each suit, MCMC is seeking RM300 million in damages, comprising RM100 million in general damages, RM100 million in aggravated damages and RM100 million in exemplary damages.
Teo said legal action against major technology companies was not unprecedented internationally.
She cited a case in the United States involving 47 state governments suing Meta over allegations that it had failed to protect children's welfare, which she said resulted in the company agreeing to a US$25 billion settlement and commitments to improve its platforms.
She said this was the first time MCMC had filed a lawsuit against Google, although similar legal action had previously been taken against messaging application Telegram.
"Such legal proceedings may take some time, but this action is certainly justified," she said.

Title: Hibiscus Petroleum Q1 net profit jumps to RM101mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hibiscus Petroleum Bhd's net profit surged to RM101.06 million in the first quarter (Q1) ended Sept 30, 2026, up from RM20.10 million a year earlier, supported by higher contributions from its operations in Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, Brunei, and the United Kingdom.
Revenue rose to RM795.15 million from RM433.06 million in the corresponding quarter last year.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the oil and gas producer said its Peninsular Malaysia segment recorded revenue of RM248.23 million, compared with RM80.55 million a year earlier, while Sabah revenue increased to RM292.01 million from RM191.23 million.
Revenue from Brunei operations increased to RM157.83 million from RM98.91 million, driven by higher gas and condensate production following the commissioning of a low-pressure compressor (LPC) at the Block B MLJ asset.
"The asset delivered a strong operational performance in the current quarter, with the LPC system operating at an average equipment uptime of 98 per cent following start-up and production in low-pressure mode, resulting in a 58 per cent increase in gas and condensate production, while production optimisation activities are ongoing," it said.
In the United Kingdom, Hibiscus Petroleum said its revenue rose to RM94.61 million from RM57.51 million, with production from the Teal West field contributing to higher output after achieving first oil on July 4.
The group declared a first interim single-tier dividend of 2.5 sen per share for the financial year ending June 30, 2027 (FY2027), up from 2.0 sen in the corresponding quarter last year.
Separately, Hibiscus Petroleum managing director Dr Kenneth Pereira said the group continues to benefit from elevated commodity prices, which contributed to the year-on-year improvement in its financial performance.
"Our Heads of Agreement with Seri Pajam Development Sdn Bhd is a milestone towards the group's diversification into energy transition and adjacent energy businesses, while keeping oil and gas at our core, in line with our Hibiscus 3.0 strategy.
"Malaysia's fast-growing power demand from data centres, including those supporting artificial intelligence (AI) workloads, will require a substantial increase in power generation supply," he said.
Pereira added that the group is continuing discussions with a potential strategic investor to secure an optimal commercial proposal and advance towards its 2030 target of achieving net production of 70,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.

Title: Aireen Omar resigned as Tune Protect's non-independent, non-executive director
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Aireen Omar has resigned as a non-independent, non-executive director of Tune Protect Group Bhd to pursue other interests, the general insurance group said, a post she had held since November 2019.
Aireen was previously with Capital A Bhd between January 2006 and December 2025. She last held the position of president of investment and ventures of Capital A between December 2021 and December 2025.
The 53-year-old was the chief executive officer of AirAsia Bhd between July 2012 and December 2017.
She started her career with Deutsche Bank Securities in New York in 1997 after completing a Bachelor of Economics degree at the London School of Economics. She also holds a Master degree in Economics from the New York University.
Aireen recently joined the board of  Zuspresso (M) Sdn Bhd, the operator of the ZUS Coffee cafe chain, as well as Billplz, a payment services for merchants.
She is also the chairperson of AI Malaysia Bhd, formerly the National AI Office.

Title: OSK's Q3 net profit edges up to RM157mil on property, cable gains
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: OSK Holdings Bhd's net profits edged up 2.91 per cent to RM156.61 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), from RM152.18 million in the corresponding quarter a year earlier, lifted by stronger earnings across its property, industrial and hospitality divisions.
Revenue for the quarter jumped 36.7 per cent year-on-year to RM678.91 million from RM496.68 million, while pre-tax profit climbed 9.6 per cent to RM180.41 million from RM164.60 million. Earnings per share stood at 5.06 sen, compared with 4.92 sen previously.
Bottom-line growth was tempered by a higher tax expense of RM22.91 million—up from RM12.58 million a year ago—alongside softer profit contributions from its investment holding and financial services operations.
"The group's diversified business portfolio delivered broad-based earnings growth, with all segments reporting improved results except the financial services and investment holding segments which recorded lower profit contributions in Q3 FY26," OSK said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today.
In a separate statement, executive chairman Tan Sri Ong Leong Huat underscored the resilience of the conglomerate's diversified business model.
"We continue to see opportunities across our businesses, even as the operating environment presents its share of challenges. Our diversified portfolio remains an important strength, allowing us to draw on the experience and capabilities of our different businesses while staying focused on our long-term ambitions," he said.
"Our priority is to keep building on what we have established, strengthen our foundations and remain disciplined in how we approach growth. With the dedication of our people and the continued support of our stakeholders, we are well positioned to take the Group forward and pursue opportunities that will contribute to its long-term success," Ong added.
The property segment was the primary earnings driver during the quarter, with pre-tax profit more than doubling—up 104.7 per cent year-on-year—to RM51.12 million from RM24.97 million, as revenue grew 28.2 per cent to RM260.31 million.
OSK attributed the surge to healthy sales momentum and steady construction progress across ongoing township and high-rise developments, including commercial shop lots in Sungai Petani, Alia and Bayu at Mori Park in Shah Alam, Hana Hills in Taman Melawati, and Iringan Bayu in Seremban.
Its property investment arm also maintained stable office performance and recorded a modest uptick in retail occupancy.
In the industries segment, revenue surged 58.55 per cent to RM291.74 million from RM184.00 million, while pre-tax profit increased 33.3 per cent to RM16.96 million from RM12.72 million.
Growth was propelled by higher cable sales volumes to both public utility and private sector clients, though margins were compressed by elevated raw material costs and ongoing losses at its Johor Bahru plants, where machinery refurbishment was still underway.
Its Acotec industrialised building system (IBS) division posted flat revenue but improved profitability on lower operating costs.
The group noted that rising raw material costs continued to weigh on the cable division's margins, "particularly in certain fixed-price contracts".
The hospitality segment saw revenue climb 8.92 per cent from a year ago to RM34.50 million and pre-tax profit rose 24.3 per cent to RM4.19 million.
The improvement reflected a full-quarter contribution from the rebranded Swiss-Grand Beach Resort Kuantan following Phase 2 refurbishment—having only reopened partially in August 2025—as well as higher revenue per available room across its hotel portfolio.
Going forward, OSK said Swiss-Grand Beach Resort Kuantan would capitalise on its five-star hotel classification to strengthen its market positioning and branding.
Conversely, pre-tax profit for the investment holding segment fell 16.7 per cent to RM76.18 million from RM91.41 million a year ago, weighed down by a lower share of profits from associate RHB Bank Bhd.
Meanwhile, the financial services segment posted an 18.5 per cent year-on-year increase in revenue to RM92.23 million as its total loan portfolio across Malaysia, Australia and Singapore expanded to approximately RM2.8 billion from RM2.7 billion a year ago.
However, segment pre-tax profit edged down 0.51 per cent to RM31.97 million from RM32.13 million after recognising a net impairment of RM14.3 million during the quarter.
Stripping out that charge, however, the division's underlying earnings grew sharply. "Without the one-off increase in impairment, this segment recorded pre-tax profit growth of 44 per cent, with pre-tax profit reaching RM46.3 million," said OSK.
For the cumulative nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, OSK's net profit rose 4.7 per cent to RM438.06 million from RM418.47 million, while revenue expanded 19.1 per cent to RM1.68 billion from RM1.41 billion.
Looking ahead, the group noted that unbilled property sales stood at RM1.7 billion as at Sept 30, backed by a 2,402-acre land bank with an estimated gross development value of RM16.4 billion.
Handovers for BLVD, Phase 2 of its Melbourne Square project in Australia—which has achieved an 82 per cent take-up rate—commenced in October, with profit recognition expected in the fourth quarter.
OSK specified that partial profit recognition from BLVD is expected starting from Q4 2026, while AURA, Phase 3 of the Melbourne Square development launched in April 2026, had recorded an encouraging 21 per cent take-up rate as at Sept 30.
Domestically, the group will keep focusing on sales conversion and delivery of launched projects while maintaining its launch pipeline, noting that OSK Ombak in Kuantan commenced sales in April 2026 alongside innovative initiatives and targeted marketing campaigns to support demand.
In financial services, demand for corporate and commercial real estate financing is expected to strengthen on the back of strategic expansion across its operating markets, while Malaysian consumer financing remains a key growth driver, with civil servant salary adjustments expected to provide a firmer foundation for expansion.
Still, the group flagged persistent macroeconomic and cost headwinds across its core businesses.
"Ongoing geopolitical tensions, uncertainties in the global trade environment and rising construction and bank borrowing interest costs remain key challenges that could compress profit margins and moderate purchaser demand," it said.
On its manufacturing operations, OSK said plant upgrades in Johor Bahru had reached an advanced stage of completion, adding: "The improved productivity and operational stability will position the group's cable division to capture Malaysia's ongoing infrastructure and energy transition investments."
With the completion of product testing and certification—particularly for high-voltage cables—the group added that it would be able to introduce new products to complement its existing range and tap into new markets moving forward.
Entering the final quarter of 2026, OSK said its immediate priorities include advancing ongoing property developments, expanding its financing portfolio, strengthening hotel performance and improving operational efficiency across the industries segment.
"While market conditions and cost pressures continue to present challenges, the group remains disciplined in managing its businesses and pursuing opportunities across its markets, focusing on sustainable growth and long-term value creation," it said.
Supported by resilient domestic demand, year-end holiday travel and ongoing infrastructure activity, the group struck an optimistic tone for the final quarter.
"Based on current performance across all business segments and barring any unforeseen circumstances, the Board is confident in delivering satisfactory results for the remaining of the financial year," it said.

Title: Country's technological rise seen in a positive light
Article:
OUTSIDE China, the country's rapid technological rise is sometimes seen as something to be feared.
On the ground in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area in South China, visiting journalists, scholars and officials from across the Asia-Pacific were recently greeted by a much more benign reality: automated ports, AI-powered grids and replicable sustainable urban development that promise to make the world a better place.
Hosting forums and field tours alongside this year's APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, the city of Shenzhen has become a testing ground for how firsthand exposure stacks up against longstanding narratives and stubborn prejudices.
Yasiru Ranaraja, founding director of the Belt and Road Initiative Sri Lanka, recently visited Guangdong's capital, Guangzhou, a hub in the Greater Bay Area.
Ranaraja, touring the Nansha Port Phase IV Fully Automated Terminal and the Guangzhou Nansha International Logistics Centre, looked at how integrating technology and logistics into international trade creates broader opportunities across the Asia-Pacific and beyond.
"It is a very modern arrangement they have done here, because in this supply-chain cargo business, what is most important is time," he said.
"That's because the ship cannot wait for a long time, so whoever can do it very efficiently can win market capacity."
Other countries should study these management models developed in China to see if they can be implemented locally, because "the benefits will go to the people of that country and the world", Ranaraja said. "That is what is important. You can get the lower prices in products, and then eventual benefit will come to your people."
After touring Shenzhen, Ranaraja said he was also impressed by the city's public spaces, including its well-furnished parks, museums and riverbank walking lanes.
"That is something good that your policymakers and government officials are doing — making public spaces much more efficient."
The economic backdrop to all this is Shenzhen's flourishing trade with APEC economies, the value of which has risen more than tenfold over 30 years, from 267.5 billion yuan (US$40.1billion) in 1996 to 3.13 trillion yuan last year, according to the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily. For international observers touring the region, street-level reality is now reflecting those figures.
On a tour of the Greater Bay Area, Aman ul Haq, controller of international relations for Pakistan Television Corporation in Islamabad,pushed back against the negative portrayal of China's technological advances as his Chinese hosts asked him whether Chinese manufacturing represented a shock or an opportunity.
"You can say it is shocking when we see this modernisation, but it is an opportunity for the world. It is very important to replicate these things."
Mark Beeson, an adjunct professor at the Australia-China Relations Institute at the University of Technology Sydney, is a frequent visitor to China who goes by the
Chinese name "Bi Sheng", meaning "surely will win".
Having first visited China in 1990, Beeson called the scale and speed of its development astounding.
[[nid:1587198]]
When he toured Shenzhen in September, he described the city as "amazing", noting it "has come from nowhere" in roughly 40 years to become "this huge city with modern architecture".
Calling China's broader trajectory "impressive", he pointed to its success in lifting tens of millions out of poverty, tackling climate change and transitioning to green energy.
Rebecca Fannin, founder of Silicon Dragon Ventures of the United States, a news, events and research group covering innovation and investment hubs, has watched firsthand how today's Chinese technology behemoths were built from scratch.
Attending the Asia-Pacific Media Forum in Shenzhen in September, she toured local high-tech exhibitions on the sidelines, where Chinese reporters asked for her take on the sector.
She pointed to global household names such as the smartphone maker Oppo and the new energy vehicle maker BYD, both based in Shenzhen.
"I remember when Oppo was a baby, and now is an adult," Fannin said. "Same thing with BYD … Now BYD is getting much more of a global presence.
"I'm happy to say that I was there from when all this was starting.
China is very effective in the business models.
We are definitely seeing this becoming a much bigger story internationally."
The spectacular rise of the artificial intelligence company DeepSeek of Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, "was a surprise to people in the West", she said.
"They didn't expect that China could do that and make a large language model that was very efficient and cost-effective.
"There was a lot of scepticism about China's innovation.
There is a new respect for China's innovation that we didn't see even 10 years ago."
In Zhuhai, Guangdong province, Anish Chand, managing digital editor of The Fiji Times, was drawn to an AI-powered inspection robotic dog during a visit to the Qinyun smart substation, a power hub linking Guangdong and the Macao Special Administrative Region.
He stopped to snap photos on his phone before squatting beside the robot for a picture with a thumbs-up.
"I have seen robots on YouTube videos, but this is the first time I have seen one live," he said.
Such technology could significantly boost industrial development in his country, he added.
Muhammad Zahir Shah, director of news at Pakistan's Bol TV, made his first visit to China this year and called its AI-hybrid engagement "revolutionary".
"Especially the green ecology, I think the same green ecology and low-carbon industry experiment can be duplicated in Pakistan. Pakistan can benefit a lot," he said.
John Wallace, an adviser at the Asia Pacific Journalism Centre in Melbourne, Australia, an organisation whose mission is to promote quality journalism, said during a recent visit to Guangdong that the notion that China poses a threat to the world gets a lot of space in Australian media.
"The thing about coming to China is you can see the genuineness and the enthusiasm of people here, to do the right thing as a global citizen — and that is a terribly important message to convey to other countries."
Wallace stressed the value of "bringing people together, providing opportunities for people from other countries to see what China is doing and how genuine it is."

Title: Proton opens RM1.5mil Bangsar e.Mas showroom

Title: Altimet lodges police report over suspected illegal foreign tenants in Lembah Jaya
Article:
AMPANG: Lembah Jaya assemblyman Altimet has lodged a police report calling for an investigation into claims that property owners in his constituency are renting out residential and commercial premises to undocumented foreigners.
Altimet, whose real name is Syed Ahmad Syed Abdul Rahman Alhadad, said the report followed numerous complaints from residents about the presence of foreigners suspected of lacking valid immigration documents or holding invalid United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cards.
He lodged the report at the Ampang police station at 3.17pm today.
He said monitoring carried out following the complaints had identified several residential and commercial premises rented out to foreigners.
"We suspect that several property owners in these neighbourhoods are renting out premises or houses to undocumented foreigners or those holding invalid UNHCR cards.
"Our hope is that the authorities investigate. We are not accusing anyone at this juncture, as these are merely suspicions.
"We will leave it to the authorities to investigate and take appropriate action," he told reporters.
Altimet said the matter could involve offences under Section 55E of the Immigration Act 1959/63, which concerns occupiers allowing undocumented immigrants to enter or remain on their premises.
He said the initiative, involving local councillors, village chiefs, neighbourhood watch committees and residents' associations, was aimed at supporting enforcement efforts by the Ampang Jaya district police headquarters.
He said he frequently received complaints from constituents through WhatsApp, social media and visits to his service centre.
Altimet also claimed that businesses operated by undocumented foreigners could affect local traders' livelihoods through unfair price competition.
"Without the necessary permits, their business operating costs are much lower, allowing them to undercut prices.
"Our local traders are the ones affected. We have many young entrepreneurs in Lembah Jaya, as well as those who have been operating sundry shops for years.
"These businesses are their livelihood, and we do not want this to become a burden on them," he said.
He said some residents had also expressed concerns over the presence of undocumented foreigners in their neighbourhoods, with some parents reluctant to allow their children to play outdoors.
However, he said he did not believe the situation was particularly serious and that social media might have amplified perceptions of the scale of the problem.
Altimet also cautioned residents against taking matters into their own hands.
"We do not want residents, in their efforts to uphold the law, to end up breaking the law themselves.
"They do not have the authority to act. That authority rests with the police and the Immigration Department," he said.
He stressed that he had no issue with foreigners residing or working in the country legally.
Meanwhile, a copy of the police report sighted by the New Straits Times listed complaints received this month from residents in Tasik Tambahan 2 and 3, Taman Sri Raya, Taman Sri Bayu and Kampung Ampang Campuran.
The report listed 19 residential premises — 16 in Taman Sri Raya and three in Taman Tasik — as well as commercial premises in Tasik Tambahan, which were claimed to be occupied by foreigners.
The immigration status of the occupants has yet to be established.

Title: Self-reform lessons
Article:
A STATE'S true strength lies not only in its ability to devise strategies and implement decisions. It also depends on whether its institutions can recognise mistakes, correct shortcomings and pursue long-term objectives despite changing circumstances.
The fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China Central Committee, which concluded on October 29, offers an opportunity to examine these capabilities.
Many developing economies struggle to turn national strategies into tangible results. Administrative weaknesses, corruption, poor coordination and policy discontinuity often undermine investments that could improve productivity and living standards.
China's experience deserves attention, not as a political blueprint, but as a case study for examining the institutions that support long-term modernisation.
One important element of the session's communique is that the Party has found two answers to escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall: the people's oversight of government and the Party's self-reform.
From an economic perspective, this highlights an essential dimension of state capacity: institutional self-correction.
China offers a useful perspective. The communique connects the strengthening of Party governance with the completion of the 14th Five-Year Plan (2021-25) and the beginning of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30). This connection reflects the importance that China's leadership attaches to strategic continuity.
Some developing countries face major infrastructure and industrial projects that often extend across several administrations. Shifts in political priorities may interrupt their implementation.
That said, changes in political leadership need not automatically dismantle national development priorities.
Static stability focuses on maintaining existing structures. Dynamic stability allows institutions to preserve strategic direction while learning, adapting and improving their performance. Dynamic stability matters more for long-term development.
No single institutional arrangement can provide a universal path to modernisation. International experience can inform domestic choices, but successful institutional reform requires adaptation rather than imitation.
China's experience encourages a wider examination of how countries can strengthen planning capabilities, improve administrative coordination and build institutions that support long-term economic transformation.
This perspective also creates opportunities for South-South cooperation. Trade, investment and infrastructure remain important, but cooperation can extend further into public administration, technical training, development planning and policy evaluation.
For the Global South, the central challenge does not require a choice between stability and transformation. It requires a country to be capable of delivering both. Ultimately, institutional resilience depends on whether good results can be continuously delivered as economic, technological and international circumstances evolve.
The author is the director of the China-Brazil Centre for Research and Business. This is an abridged version of an article that appeared in China Daily. The views do not necessarily reflect those of China Daily.

Title: Trade pact 3.0 to lift ties with Asean
Article:
CHINA and its Southeast Asian neighbours should take the entry into force of the China-Asean Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol as an opportunity to deepen industrial and supply chain cooperation and boost connectivity, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said at the 29th China-Asean Summit.
The gathering was held on November 16 in Manila, the Philippines, where the two sides announced that the China-Asean FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, signed in October last year, will enter into force on December 1.
The two sides should accelerate infrastructure connectivity, or "hard connectivity", in areas such as railways and highways, and strengthen "soft connectivity" in mechanisms, standards and rules, Li said.
China has been Asean's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, and Asean has been China's largest trading partner for six consecutive years.
From January through July this year, trade between China and Asean was worth US$744.41 billion, up 24.7 per cent from the same period last year, according to the Ministry of Commerce.
Xu Liping, director of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Centre for Southeast Asian Studies, said that the upgrade of the China-Asean FTA will "significantly accelerate the pace of institutional opening-up on both sides".
"Both sides are actively leading the shaping of international rules in emerging areas such as the digital economy, the green economy, e-commerce supply chain connectivity and consumer protection, further boosting two-way growth in investment and trade," he said.
The upgrade builds on earlier trade and investment liberalisation and facilitation by deepening the coordination of regional rules and standards, according to a Ministry of Commerce official.
For example, the protocol encourages the two sides to recognise each other's conformity assessment results to reduce the time and expense of duplicate testing and certification across regional markets."For businesses, this can do more to enhance the competitiveness of their products than tariff preferences alone," the official said.
Under the protocol, collaboration on electronic invoicing, payments and bills of lading will improve system compatibility and cut business costs, the official said, adding that digital collaboration will extend to artificial intelligence.
The upgrade reflects both sides' commitment to multilateralism and free trade, and will give fresh impetus to Asia-Pacific economic integration amid global economic and trade uncertainty, the commerce ministry said.
To help businesses benefit from the new arrangements, the ministry will organise targeted training and work with Asean to advance practical collaboration, including further consultation on the digital economy and AI.
The meeting also designated 2027 as the China-Asean Year of AI cooperation.
Other outcome documents issued covered topics such as the fifth anniversary of the establishment of the China-Asean comprehensive strategic partnership, the founding of an energy cooperation partnership and the deepening of forestry cooperation, according to China's Foreign Ministry.
Li said that China applauds the establishment of a China-Asean mechanism for energy ministers' meetings and stands ready to work with Asean to successfully hold the China-Asean Year of AI cooperation in 2027, advance "AI plus" cooperation and create a strong engine for high-quality regional economic development.
He called on China and Asean countries to protect and develop their common home, injecting greater stability and certainty into the development and prosperity of the global village.
He also urged the two sides to strengthen the foundations for peace and security by properly handling differences through dialogue and consultation, jointly opposing external interference and safeguarding regional peace and stability.
Referring to the China-Asean comprehensive strategic partnership, Li said that these extraordinary five years and the hard-won achievements offer valuable experience and useful lessons.
Both sides need to carry forward their tradition of friendship and mutual assistance, uphold the right path of openness and win-win cooperation, and keep pace with the trend of innovation and development, he said.

Title: Canada's parliament receives petition to oust Trump's envoy
Article:
MONTREAL: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's administration will have until January to respond to a petition with nearly 300,000 signatures introduced to parliament this week demanding the removal of US Ambassador Pete Hoekstra.
The United States and Canada remain locked in a trade war, although Carney and US President Donald Trump have both expressed optimism that talks are progressing despite making similar comments days before similar negotiations collapsed in August.
Hoekstra, a relentless Trump defender and a former Republican congressman from Michigan, has had a volatile tenure since his arrival in Canada in April 2025.
Canada's Green Party lawmaker, Elizabeth May, who tabled the petition in the House of Commons on Wednesday, branded Hoekstra "the most undiplomatic diplomat."
"I think it's important to note that Canadians overwhelmingly have, on this e-petition, spoken clearly that they believe that Pete Hoekstra is not welcome in Canada," she said.
May said Hoekstra had been "repeatedly abusive and insulting to Canadians", stressing that more than 280,000 Canadians had "asked the government... to declare him officially persona non grata and revoke his rights to operate as a diplomat" in the country.
Petitions presented in the House of Commons require a formal government response within 45 days.
The citizen-led petition, which was open for signature until November 18, accused Hoekstra of normalizing "the Trump administration's threats to annex Canada as the 51st state."
Hoekstra reportedly levelled a profanity-laced tirade against an Ontario official over an anti-tariff ad that quoted former US president Ronald Reagan on the merits of free trade.
The ad, produced by Ontario's provincial government, infuriated Trump, prompting him to suspend all trade negotiations.
Hoekstra said in June that the idea of the United States annexing Canada would be "a great discussion" for Trump to have with Carney.
He has also defended Trump's tariffs and criticized Canadians for referring to the US president's protectionist measures as being part of a trade war.
Canada wants relief from tariffs on key sectors, notably autos, but Ottawa has warned that completely removing the levies is unlikely and that the Canadian economy needs to adjust to a permanently altered trading relationship with the United States.

Title: TM ventures into advanced robotics with AGIBOT, Swancor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Telekom Malaysia Bhd (TM) is venturing into advanced robotics through separate collaborations with AGIBOT Innovation (Shanghai) Technology Co Ltd (AGIBOT) and Swancor Advanced Materials Co Ltd (Swancor) to develop Malaysia's robotics ecosystem and commercialise robotics solutions for Malaysian consumers and businesses.
TM said in a statement today that under its collaboration with AGIBOT, TM will serve as AGIBOT's exclusive sovereign advanced robotics platform provider in Malaysia.
"The platform will enable the secure and scalable deployment, integration and localisation of AGIBOT's robotics technologies, robotics models and software, reinforcing Malaysia's digital sovereignty.
"For enterprises, the collaboration will explore extending TM One's Vision artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities with autonomous mobile robots that can patrol beyond fixed-camera coverage, respond to alerts and assist with routine maintenance under remote supervision," it said.
TM said that for data centres, potential applications include autonomous robotic inspection and monitoring to support predictive maintenance and improve operational efficiency. Specific solutions will be determined through demand-led market validation and technical development.
The AGIBOT collaboration will also explore joint research, technical training and knowledge transfer through TM Research and Development and Multimedia University.
Meanwhile, under its collaboration with Swancor Advanced Materials, TM will serve as Swancor's market and commercialisation partner for advanced consumer robots in Malaysia.
"Leveraging Unifi's reach across 3.2 million broadband subscribers, TM aims to introduce advanced home companion robots as part of its Smart Home ecosystem.
"These robots could support household safety, well-being, learning and everyday family needs, contributing to safer, smarter and more connected homes," it said.
TM group chief executive officer Datuk Amar Huzaimi Md Deris said the strategic collaborations would allow TM to build on its strengths in connectivity and cloud infrastructure, extend its digital capabilities into new applications and create greater value from its existing infrastructure.
"Our ambition is to shape Malaysia's advanced robotics ecosystem, bringing together global technology and local capabilities to develop solutions that are genuinely useful, safe and suited to the needs of Malaysians.
"Through these collaborations, we aim to accelerate the adoption of advanced robotics, develop local talent and contribute to Malaysia's digital aspiration," he said.
